title.zh: 卷105之一 天象志一之一
title.raw: 卷105之一 天象志一之一 Volume 105a Treatise 1: Celestial Phenomena 1

sentences.zh: 夫在天成象，聖人是觀，日月五星，象之著者，變常舛度，徵咎隨焉。

translations.literal: Now, images are formed in Heaven; the sage observes them. The sun, moon, and five planets are the most prominent of these images; when their regular motions depart from the norm, signs of calamity follow.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven forms images for men to read, and the sage watches them. The sun, moon, and five planets are the clearest of these signs; when their courses stray from the norm, omens of disaster follow in turn.

sentences.zh: 然則明晦暈蝕，疾餘犯守，飛流欻起，彗孛不恒，或皇靈降臨，示譴以戒下，或王化有虧，感達於天路。

translations.literal: Thus brightness and dimness, halos and eclipses, swift motion and lingering, conjunction and stationary positions, shooting stars that rise suddenly, and comets that appear without regularity—sometimes the imperial numen descends to display reproof and warn those below, sometimes the kingly transformation suffers loss and the response reaches the heavenly paths.
translations.idiomatic: Brightness and dimness, halos and eclipses, swift passages and lingering stations, planetary conjunctions, shooting stars that flare up without warning, and comets that appear at no fixed season—all of this may mean that the imperial spirit has descended to show reproof and warn the realm below, or that the kingly transformation has faltered and Heaven has answered along the celestial roads.

sentences.zh: 易稱「天垂象，見吉凶」，「觀乎天文，以察時變」；

translations.literal: The Changes says, "Heaven hangs forth images, revealing fortune and misfortune," and "Observe the patterns of Heaven to examine the changes of the times";
translations.idiomatic: The Changes says that Heaven displays images by which fortune and misfortune may be seen, and that one should observe the patterns of Heaven to discern how the times are changing;

sentences.zh: 書曰「曆象日月星辰，敬授民時」。

translations.literal: The Documents says, "Calculate and image the sun, moon, stars, and constellations, and respectfully bestow the seasons upon the people."
translations.idiomatic: the Documents says that one must calculate and chart the sun, moon, stars, and constellations and respectfully hand down the seasons to the people.

sentences.zh: 是故有國有家者之所祗畏也。

translations.literal: Therefore this is what those who possess a state or a family hold in reverent awe.
translations.idiomatic: That is why every lord of state and house holds these matters in reverent awe.

sentences.zh: 百王興廢之驗，萬國禍福之來，兆勤雖微，罔不必至，著於前載，不可得而備舉也。

translations.literal: The verification of the rise and fall of the hundred kings, the coming of fortune and misfortune to the myriad states—though the omen may be slight and the exertion small, none fails to arrive in the end. Recorded in earlier annals, they cannot all be enumerated in full.
translations.idiomatic: The proof of how the hundred kings rose and fell, and how fortune and disaster came to the myriad states, shows that even the slightest omen, however faint, was sure to be fulfilled in the end. Earlier records preserve these events, though they cannot all be listed here.

sentences.zh: 班史以日暈五星之屬列天文志，薄蝕彗孛之比入五行說。

translations.literal: Ban Gu's history placed solar halos, the five planets, and the like in the Treatise on Astronomy, while thin eclipses, comets, and similar phenomena were entered into the discourse on the Five Phases.
translations.idiomatic: In Ban Gu's history, solar halos and the five planets were set out in the Treatise on Astronomy, whereas eclipses, comets, and related phenomena were folded into the discussion of the Five Phases.

sentences.zh: 七曜一也，而分為二志，故陸機云學者所疑也。

translations.literal: The seven luminaries are one subject, yet they were divided into two treatises; therefore Lu Ji said that scholars have doubted this.
translations.idiomatic: The seven luminaries are really one subject, yet they were split across two treatises, which is why Lu Ji said scholars have long found this arrangement doubtful.

sentences.zh: 今以在天諸異咸入天象，其應徵符合，隨而條載，無所顯驗則闕之云。

translations.literal: Now all celestial anomalies are entered into the Treatise on Celestial Phenomena; where there are corresponding confirmations, they are recorded item by item, and where there is no clear verification, that is noted as omitted.
translations.idiomatic: Here all anomalies in the heavens are gathered into the Treatise on Celestial Phenomena. Where a corresponding event can be confirmed, it is recorded in sequence; where no clear verification exists, the entry is left blank.

sentences.zh: 太祖天興五年八月，天鳴。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor, Tianxing fifth year, eighth month: the sky roared.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of Tianxing 5, under Emperor Daozu, the sky roared.

sentences.zh: 六年九月，天鳴。

translations.literal: Sixth year, ninth month: the sky roared.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the sixth year, the sky roared again.

sentences.zh: 皇始二年十月壬辰，日暈，有佩璚。

translations.literal: Huangshi second year, tenth month, renchen day: a solar halo appeared, with pendant halos.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen in the tenth month of Huangshi 2, the sun was ringed by a halo with pendant rings.

sentences.zh: 占曰「兵起」。

translations.literal: Prognostication: "Warfare will arise."
translations.idiomatic: The prognostication read: "Warfare will arise."

sentences.zh: 天興元年九月，烏丸張超收合亡命，聚黨三千餘家，據勃海之南皮，自號征東大將軍、烏丸王，鈔掠諸郡。

translations.literal: Tianxing first year, ninth month: the Wuhuan Zhang Chao gathered fugitives, assembled a faction of more than three thousand households, seized Nanpi in Bohai, styled himself Grand General Who Conquers the East and King of the Wuhuan, and raided the commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of Tianxing 1, the Wuhuan leader Zhang Chao rallied fugitives into a force of more than three thousand households, seized Nanpi in Bohai, proclaimed himself Grand General Who Conquers the East and King of the Wuhuan, and raided the surrounding commanderies.

sentences.zh: 詔將軍庾岳討之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered General Yu Yue to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered General Yu Yue to campaign against him.

sentences.zh: 天興三年六月庚辰朔，日有蝕之。

translations.literal: Tianxing third year, sixth month, gengchen new moon: there was an eclipse of the sun.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengchen new moon in the sixth month of Tianxing 3, a solar eclipse occurred.

sentences.zh: 占曰「外國侵，土地分」。

translations.literal: Prognostication: "Foreign states will invade, and territory will be divided."
translations.idiomatic: The prognostication read: "Foreign powers will invade, and territory will be divided."

sentences.zh: 五年五月，姚興遣其弟義陽公平率眾四萬來侵平陽，乾壁為平所陷。

translations.literal: Fifth year, fifth month: Yao Xing sent his younger brother, Prince of Yiyang Yao Ping, leading forty thousand men to invade Pingyang; Ganbi was taken by Ping.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the fifth year, Yao Xing sent his brother Yao Ping, Prince of Yiyang, at the head of forty thousand men to invade Pingyang, and Ganbi fell to Ping.

sentences.zh: 六年四月癸巳朔，日有蝕之。

translations.literal: Sixth year, fourth month, guisi new moon: there was an eclipse of the sun.
translations.idiomatic: On the guisi new moon in the fourth month of the sixth year, a solar eclipse occurred.

sentences.zh: 占曰「兵稍出」。

translations.literal: Prognostication: "Armies will gradually emerge."
translations.idiomatic: The prognostication read: "Armies will gradually take the field."

sentences.zh: 十月，太祖詔將軍伊謂率騎二萬北襲高車，大破之。

translations.literal: Tenth month: the Founding Emperor ordered General Yi Wei to lead twenty thousand horsemen in a northern strike against the Gaoche and inflicted a great defeat upon them.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month, Emperor Daozu ordered General Yi Wei to lead twenty thousand cavalry in a northern raid against the Gaoche and routed them decisively.

sentences.zh: 天賜五年七月戊戌朔，日有蝕之。

translations.literal: Tianci fifth year, seventh month, wuxu new moon: there was an eclipse of the sun.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuxu new moon in the seventh month of Tianci 5, a solar eclipse occurred.

sentences.zh: 占曰「后死」。

translations.literal: Prognostication: "The empress will die."
translations.idiomatic: The prognostication read: "The empress will die."

sentences.zh: 六年七月，夫人劉氏薨，後諡為宣穆皇后。

translations.literal: Sixth year, seventh month: Lady Liu died; she was later given the posthumous title Empress Xuanmu.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the sixth year, Lady Liu died and was later posthumously titled Empress Xuanmu.

sentences.zh: 太宗神瑞二年八月庚辰晦，日有蝕之。

translations.literal: Emperor Mingyuan, Shenrui second year, eighth month, gengchen last day of the month: there was an eclipse of the sun.
translations.idiomatic: On the last day of the eighth month of Shenrui 2, under Emperor Mingyuan, a solar eclipse occurred.

sentences.zh: 世祖始光四年六月癸卯朔，日有蝕之。

translations.literal: Emperor Taiwu, Shiguang fourth year, sixth month, guimao new moon: there was an eclipse of the sun.
translations.idiomatic: On the guimao new moon in the sixth month of Shiguang 4, under Emperor Taiwu, a solar eclipse occurred.

sentences.zh: 占曰「諸侯非其人」。

translations.literal: Prognostication: "The feudal lords are not the right men."
translations.idiomatic: The prognostication read: "The feudal lords are not the right men for their posts."

sentences.zh: 神䴥元年二月，司空奚斤、監軍侍御史安頡討赫連昌，擒之於安定。

translations.literal: Shenlu first year, second month: Minister of Works Xi Jin and Supervisory Army Attendant Censor An Ji campaigned against Helian Chang and captured him at Anding.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Shenlu 1, Minister of Works Xi Jin and Supervisory Army Attendant Censor An Ji campaigned against Helian Chang and captured him at Anding.

sentences.zh: 其餘眾立昌弟定為主，走還平涼，斤追之，為定所擒。

translations.literal: The remaining forces set up Chang's younger brother Ding as their leader and fled back to Pingliang; Jin pursued them and was captured by Ding.
translations.idiomatic: The survivors enthroned Chang's younger brother Ding and fled to Pingliang. Jin pursued them and was captured by Ding.

sentences.zh: 將軍丘堆棄甲與守將高涼王禮東走蒲坂，世祖怒，斬堆。

translations.literal: General Qiu Dui cast off his armor and, together with the defending commander Prince of Gaoliang Tuoba Li, fled east to Puban; the Emperor was enraged and executed Dui.
translations.idiomatic: General Qiu Dui abandoned his armor and fled east to Puban with the defending commander, Prince of Gaoliang Tuoba Li. Emperor Taiwu was furious and had Dui executed.

sentences.zh: 神䴥元年十一月乙未朔，日有蝕之。

translations.literal: Shenlu first year, eleventh month, yiwei new moon: there was an eclipse of the sun.
translations.idiomatic: On the yiwei new moon in the eleventh month of Shenlu 1, a solar eclipse occurred.

sentences.zh: 太延元年正月己未朔，日有蝕之。

translations.literal: Taiyan first year, first month, jiwei new moon: there was an eclipse of the sun.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiwei new moon in the first month of Taiyan 1, a solar eclipse occurred.

sentences.zh: 四年十一月丁卯朔，日有蝕之。

translations.literal: Fourth year, eleventh month, dingmao new moon: there was an eclipse of the sun.
translations.idiomatic: On the dingmao new moon in the eleventh month of the fourth year, a solar eclipse occurred.

sentences.zh: 太平真君元年四月戊午朔，日有蝕之。

translations.literal: Taiping Zhenjun first year, fourth month, wuwu new moon: there was an eclipse of the sun.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuwu new moon in the fourth month of Taiping Zhenjun 1, a solar eclipse occurred.

sentences.zh: 三年八月甲戌晦，日有蝕之。

translations.literal: Third year, eighth month, jiaxu last day of the month: there was an eclipse of the sun.
translations.idiomatic: On the last day of the eighth month in the third year, a solar eclipse occurred.

sentences.zh: 六年六月戊子朔，日有蝕之。

translations.literal: Sixth year, sixth month, wuzi new moon: there was an eclipse of the sun.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuzi new moon in the sixth month of the sixth year, a solar eclipse occurred.

sentences.zh: 占曰「有九族夷滅」。

translations.literal: Prognostication: "The nine degrees of kin will be exterminated to the last."
translations.idiomatic: The prognostication read: "An entire clan will be exterminated to the last."

sentences.zh: 七年正月戊辰，世祖車駕次東雍州。

translations.literal: Seventh year, first month, wuchen day: the Emperor's carriage halted at Eastern Yong Province.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen in the first month of the seventh year, Emperor Taiwu's carriage halted at Eastern Yong Province.

sentences.zh: 庚午，圍薛永宗營壘。

translations.literal: Gengwu day: he besieged Xue Yongzong's encampment.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu he besieged Xue Yongzong's camp.

sentences.zh: 永宗出戰，大敗，六軍乘之，永宗眾潰，斬永宗，男女無少長皆赴汾水而死。

translations.literal: Yongzong came out to give battle and suffered a great defeat; the six armies pressed the pursuit, Yongzong's forces collapsed, Yongzong was beheaded, and men and women, young and old alike, all threw themselves into the Fen River and died.
translations.idiomatic: Yongzong came out to fight and was routed. The six armies pressed the attack, his force collapsed, and he was beheaded. Men and women, young and old alike, threw themselves into the Fen River and drowned.

sentences.zh: 七年六月癸未朔，日有蝕之。

translations.literal: Seventh year, sixth month, guiwei new moon: there was an eclipse of the sun.
translations.idiomatic: On the guiwei new moon in the sixth month of the seventh year, a solar eclipse occurred.

sentences.zh: 占曰「不臣欲殺」。

translations.literal: Prognostication: "A subject who is not loyal seeks to kill."
translations.idiomatic: The prognostication read: "A disloyal subject will attempt murder."

sentences.zh: 八年三月，河西王沮渠牧犍謀反，伏誅。

translations.literal: Eighth year, third month: the King of Hexi, Juqu Mujian, plotted rebellion and was executed.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the eighth year, Juqu Mujian, King of Hexi, plotted rebellion and was executed.

sentences.zh: 十年夏四月丙申朔，日有蝕之。

translations.literal: Tenth year, summer, fourth month, bingshen new moon: there was an eclipse of the sun.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingshen new moon in the fourth month of summer in the tenth year, a solar eclipse occurred.

sentences.zh: 六月庚寅朔，日有蝕之。

translations.literal: Sixth month, gengyin new moon: there was an eclipse of the sun.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengyin new moon in the sixth month, a solar eclipse occurred.

sentences.zh: 占曰「將相誅」。

translations.literal: Prognostication: "Generals and ministers will be executed."
translations.idiomatic: The prognostication read: "Generals and ministers will be executed."

sentences.zh: 十一年六月己亥，誅司徒崔浩。

translations.literal: Eleventh year, sixth month, jihai day: Minister of Education Cui Hao was executed.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai in the sixth month of the eleventh year, Minister of Education Cui Hao was executed.

sentences.zh: 十一年十二月辛未，日南北有珥。

translations.literal: Eleventh year, twelfth month, xinwei day: the sun had luminous appendages to north and south.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei in the twelfth month of the eleventh year, luminous appendages appeared to the north and south of the sun.

sentences.zh: 高宗興安元年十一月己卯，日出赤如血。

translations.literal: Emperor Wencheng, Xing'an first year, eleventh month, jimao day: the sun rose red as blood.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao in the eleventh month of Xing'an 1, under Emperor Wencheng, the sun rose blood-red.

sentences.zh: 二年三月，日暈。

translations.literal: Second year, third month: a solar halo.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the second year, the sun was ringed by a halo.

sentences.zh: 興光元年七月丙申朔，日有蝕之。

translations.literal: Xingguang first year, seventh month, bingshen new moon: there was an eclipse of the sun.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingshen new moon in the seventh month of Xingguang 1, a solar eclipse occurred.

sentences.zh: 和平元年九月庚申朔，日有蝕之。

translations.literal: Heping first year, ninth month, gengshen new moon: there was an eclipse of the sun.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengshen new moon in the ninth month of Heping 1, a solar eclipse occurred.

sentences.zh: 三年二月壬子朔，日有蝕之。

translations.literal: Third year, second month, renzi new moon: there was an eclipse of the sun.
translations.idiomatic: On the renzi new moon in the second month of the third year, a solar eclipse occurred.

sentences.zh: 占曰「有白衣之會」。

translations.literal: Prognostication: "There will be a gathering in white garments."
translations.idiomatic: The prognostication read: "There will be a gathering in mourning white."

sentences.zh: 六年五月癸卯，高宗崩。

translations.literal: Sixth year, fifth month, guimao day: Emperor Wencheng died.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao in the fifth month of the sixth year, Emperor Wencheng died.

sentences.zh: 顯祖皇興元年十月己卯朔，日有蝕之。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianwen, Huangxing first year, tenth month, jimao new moon: there was an eclipse of the sun.
translations.idiomatic: On the jimao new moon in the tenth month of Huangxing 1, under Emperor Xianwen, a solar eclipse occurred.

sentences.zh: 二年四月丙子朔，日有蝕之。

translations.literal: Second year, fourth month, bingzi new moon: there was an eclipse of the sun.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingzi new moon in the fourth month of the second year, a solar eclipse occurred.

sentences.zh: 占曰「將誅」。

translations.literal: Prognostication: "A general will be executed."
translations.idiomatic: The prognostication read: "A general will be executed."

sentences.zh: 四年十月，誅濟南王慕容白曜。

translations.literal: Fourth year, tenth month: Prince of Jinan Murong Baiyao was executed.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the fourth year, Murong Baiyao, Prince of Jinan, was executed.

sentences.zh: 十月癸酉朔，日有蝕之。

translations.literal: Tenth month, guiyou new moon: there was an eclipse of the sun.
translations.idiomatic: On the guiyou new moon in the tenth month, a solar eclipse occurred.

sentences.zh: 占曰「尊后有憂」。

translations.literal: Prognostication: "The honored consort will suffer distress."
translations.idiomatic: The prognostication read: "The honored consort will face calamity."

sentences.zh: 三年，夫人李氏薨，後諡思皇后。

translations.literal: Third year: Lady Li died; she was later given the posthumous title Empress Si.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, Lady Li died and was later posthumously titled Empress Si.

sentences.zh: 三年十月丁酉朔，日有蝕之。

translations.literal: Third year, tenth month, dingyou new moon: there was an eclipse of the sun.
translations.idiomatic: On the dingyou new moon in the tenth month of the third year, a solar eclipse occurred.

sentences.zh: 高祖延興元年十二月癸卯，日有蝕之。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen, Yanxing first year, twelfth month, guimao day: there was an eclipse of the sun.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao in the twelfth month of Yanxing 1, under Emperor Xiaowen, a solar eclipse occurred.

sentences.zh: [1]占曰「有兵」。

translations.literal: [1] Prognostication: "There will be warfare."
translations.idiomatic: [1] The prognostication read: "Warfare will arise."

sentences.zh: 二年正月乙卯，統萬鎮胡民相率北叛，遣寧南將軍、交阯公韓拔等滅之。

translations.literal: Second year, first month, yimao day: the Hu people of Tongwan garrison rose in rebellion together and fled north; the court sent Defender of the South General and Duke of Jiaozhi Han Ba and others to destroy them.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao in the first month of the second year, the Hu people of Tongwan garrison rebelled together and fled north. The court sent Defender of the South General Han Ba, Duke of Jiaozhi, and others to destroy them.

sentences.zh: 三年十二月癸卯朔，日有蝕之。

translations.literal: Third year, twelfth month, guimao new moon: there was an eclipse of the sun.
translations.idiomatic: On the guimao new moon in the twelfth month of the third year, a solar eclipse occurred.

sentences.zh: 四年正月癸酉朔，日有蝕之。

translations.literal: Fourth year, first month, guiyou new moon: there was an eclipse of the sun.
translations.idiomatic: On the guiyou new moon in the first month of the fourth year, a solar eclipse occurred.

sentences.zh: [2]占曰「有崩主，天下改服。

translations.literal: [2] Prognostication: "The ruler will die, and all under Heaven will change garments of mourning.
translations.idiomatic: [2] The prognostication read: "The ruler will die, and the realm will put on mourning garments.

sentences.zh: 有大臣死」。

translations.literal: A great minister will die."
translations.idiomatic: A great minister will die as well."

sentences.zh: 五年十二月己丑，征北大將軍城陽王壽薨。

translations.literal: Fifth year, twelfth month, jichou day: Grand General Who Conquers the North, Prince of Chengyang Tuoba Shou, died.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou in the twelfth month of the fifth year, Tuoba Shou, Prince of Chengyang and Grand General Who Conquers the North, died.

sentences.zh: 六年六月辛未，顯祖崩。

translations.literal: Sixth year, sixth month, xinwei day: Emperor Xianwen died.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei in the sixth month of the sixth year, Emperor Xianwen died.

sentences.zh: 七月丙寅，日有背珥。

translations.literal: Seventh month, bingyin day: the sun had contrary luminous appendages.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin in the seventh month, contrary luminous appendages appeared beside the sun.

sentences.zh: 五年正月丁酉，白虹貫日，直珥一。

translations.literal: Fifth year, first month, dingyou day: a white rainbow pierced the sun, with one straight luminous appendage.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou in the first month of the fifth year, a white rainbow pierced the sun, with one straight luminous appendage.

sentences.zh: 承明元年三月辛卯，日暈五重，有二珥。

translations.literal: Chengming first year, third month, xinmao day: a solar halo of five rings, with two luminous appendages.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao in the third month of Chengming 1, the sun was ringed by a fivefold halo with two luminous appendages.

sentences.zh: 太和元年冬十月辛亥朔，日有蝕之。

translations.literal: Taihe first year, winter, tenth month, xinhai new moon: there was an eclipse of the sun.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinhai new moon in the tenth month of winter in Taihe 1, a solar eclipse occurred.

sentences.zh: 二年正月辛亥，日暈，東西有珥。

translations.literal: Second year, first month, xinhai day: a solar halo, with luminous appendages to east and west.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai in the first month of the second year, the sun was ringed by a halo with luminous appendages to the east and west.

sentences.zh: 二月乙酉晦，日有蝕之。

translations.literal: Second month, yiyou last day of the month: there was an eclipse of the sun.
translations.idiomatic: On the last day of the second month, a solar eclipse occurred.

sentences.zh: [3]占曰「有欲反者，近三月，遠三年」。

translations.literal: [3] Prognostication: "There are those who wish to rebel; within three months at the nearest, within three years at the farthest."
translations.idiomatic: [3] The prognostication read: "Rebels are plotting; the nearest fulfillment will come within three months, the farthest within three years."

sentences.zh: 四年正月癸卯，洮陽羌叛，枹罕鎮將討平之。

translations.literal: Fourth year, first month, guimao day: the Qiang of Taoyang rebelled; the garrison commander of Fuhan suppressed and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao in the first month of the fourth year, the Qiang of Taoyang rebelled, and the garrison commander of Fuhan suppressed them.

sentences.zh: 九月乙巳朔，日有蝕之。

translations.literal: Ninth month, yisi new moon: there was an eclipse of the sun.
translations.idiomatic: On the yisi new moon in the ninth month, a solar eclipse occurred.

sentences.zh: 占曰「東邦發兵」。

translations.literal: Prognostication: "The eastern states will raise armies."
translations.idiomatic: The prognostication read: "The eastern regions will raise armies."

sentences.zh: 四年十月丁未，蘭陵民桓富殺其縣令，與昌慮桓和北連太山羣盜張和顏等，聚黨保五固，推司馬朗之為主，詔淮陽王尉元等討之。

translations.literal: Fourth year, tenth month, dingwei day: the commoner Huan Fu of Lanling killed his county magistrate; together with Huan He of Changlu and the bandit chiefs of Mount Tai, Zhang He and Yan, and others, he gathered a faction, held Wugu, and set up Sima Langzhi as their leader. An edict ordered Prince of Huaiyang Yu Yuan and others to campaign against them.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei in the tenth month of the fourth year, Huan Fu of Lanling killed his county magistrate. Together with Huan He of Changlu and the Mount Tai bandits Zhang He, Yan, and others, he gathered a force, held Wugu, and set up Sima Langzhi as their leader. The court ordered Prince of Huaiyang Yu Yuan and others to campaign against them.

sentences.zh: 三年春正月癸丑，日暈，東西有珥，有佩戟一重，北有偃戟四重，後有白氣貫日珥，狀如車輪。

translations.literal: Third year, spring, first month, guichou day: a solar halo, with luminous appendages to east and west, one layer of pendant halberds, four layers of reclining halberds to the north, and afterward white vapor piercing the sun's halo and appendages in the shape of a carriage wheel.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou in the first month of spring in the third year, the sun was ringed by a halo with luminous appendages to the east and west, one layer of pendant halberds, four layers of reclining halberds to the north, and then white vapor pierced the halo and appendages in the shape of a carriage wheel.

sentences.zh: 京師不見，雍州以聞。

translations.literal: It was not seen in the capital; Yong Province reported it.
translations.idiomatic: The capital did not see it; Yong Province reported the phenomenon.

sentences.zh: 三月癸卯朔，日有蝕之。

translations.literal: Third month, guimao new moon: there was an eclipse of the sun.
translations.idiomatic: On the guimao new moon in the third month, a solar eclipse occurred.

sentences.zh: 占曰「大臣誅」。

translations.literal: Prognostication: "A great minister will be executed."
translations.idiomatic: The prognostication read: "A great minister will be executed."

sentences.zh: 四月，雍州刺史宜都王目辰有罪，賜死。

translations.literal: Fourth month: Tuoba Muchen, Prince of Yidu and Governor of Yong Province, was guilty and was granted death.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month, Tuoba Muchen, Prince of Yidu and governor of Yong Province, was found guilty and ordered to take his own life.

sentences.zh: 四年正月辛酉，日東西有珥，北有佩，日暈貫兩珥。

translations.literal: Fourth year, first month, xinyou day: the sun had luminous appendages to east and west and pendant halos to the north; a solar halo pierced both appendages.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou in the first month of the fourth year, luminous appendages appeared to the east and west of the sun and pendant halos to the north, and a solar halo pierced both appendages.

sentences.zh: 五年正月庚辰，日暈，東西有珥；

translations.literal: Fifth year, first month, gengchen day: a solar halo, with luminous appendages to east and west;
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen in the first month of the fifth year, the sun was ringed by a halo with luminous appendages to the east and west;

sentences.zh: 南北並白氣，長一丈，廣二尺許；

translations.literal: to north and south there were also white vapors, one zhang long and about two chi wide;
translations.idiomatic: to the north and south white vapors appeared as well, one zhang long and about two chi wide;

sentences.zh: 北有連環暈。

translations.literal: to the north there was a linked chain of halos.
translations.idiomatic: to the north there was a chain of linked halos.

sentences.zh: 又貫珥內，復有直氣，長三丈許，內黃，中青，外白。

translations.literal: Again it pierced within the appendages, and there was also a straight vapor about three zhang long, yellow within, green in the middle, and white without.
translations.idiomatic: It also pierced within the appendages, and a straight vapor about three zhang long appeared, yellow within, green in the middle, and white without.

sentences.zh: 暈乍成，散，乃滅。

translations.literal: The halo formed suddenly, dispersed, and then vanished.
translations.idiomatic: The halo formed suddenly, then dispersed and vanished.

sentences.zh: 七月庚申朔，日有蝕之。

translations.literal: Seventh month, gengshen new moon: there was an eclipse of the sun.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengshen new moon in the seventh month, a solar eclipse occurred.

sentences.zh: 七年十二月乙巳朔，日有蝕之。

translations.literal: Seventh year, twelfth month, yisi new moon: there was an eclipse of the sun.
translations.idiomatic: On the yisi new moon in the twelfth month of the seventh year, a solar eclipse occurred.

sentences.zh: 八年正月戊寅，有白氣貫日。

translations.literal: Eighth year, first month, wuyin day: white vapor pierced the sun.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin in the first month of the eighth year, white vapor pierced the sun.

sentences.zh: 占曰「近臣亂」。

translations.literal: Prognostication: "Close ministers will cause disorder."
translations.idiomatic: The prognostication read: "Close ministers will cause disorder."

sentences.zh: 十年三月丁亥，中散梁眾保等謀反，伏誅。

translations.literal: Tenth year, third month, dinghai day: Palace Attendant Liang Zhongbao and others plotted rebellion and were executed.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai in the third month of the tenth year, Palace Attendant Liang Zhongbao and others plotted rebellion and were executed.

sentences.zh: 十一年十一月丁亥，日失色。

translations.literal: Eleventh year, eleventh month, dinghai day: the sun lost its color.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai in the eleventh month of the eleventh year, the sun lost its color.

sentences.zh: 十二年三月戊戌，白虹貫日。

translations.literal: Twelfth year, third month, wuxu day: a white rainbow pierced the sun.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu in the third month of the twelfth year, a white rainbow pierced the sun.

sentences.zh: 十三年二月乙亥朔，日十五分蝕八。

translations.literal: Thirteenth year, second month, yihai new moon: the sun was eclipsed eight parts in fifteen.
translations.idiomatic: On the yihai new moon in the second month of the thirteenth year, the sun was eclipsed by eight-fifteenths of its disk.

sentences.zh: 占曰「有白衣之會」。

translations.literal: Prognostication: "There will be a gathering in white garments."
translations.idiomatic: The prognostication read: "There will be a gathering in mourning white."

sentences.zh: 十一月己未，安豐王猛薨。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, jiwei day: Prince of Anfeng Tuoba Meng died.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei in the eleventh month, Tuoba Meng, Prince of Anfeng, died.

sentences.zh: 十四年二月己巳朔未時，雲氣班駁，日十五分蝕一。

translations.literal: Fourteenth year, second month, jisi new moon, wei hour: cloud vapor was mottled, and the sun was eclipsed one part in fifteen.
translations.idiomatic: At the wei hour on the jisi new moon in the second month of the fourteenth year, mottled clouds gathered, and the sun was eclipsed by one-fifteenth of its disk.

sentences.zh: 占曰「有白衣之會」。

translations.literal: Prognostication: "There will be a gathering in white garments."
translations.idiomatic: The prognostication read: "There will be a gathering in mourning white."

sentences.zh: 九月癸丑，文明太皇太后馮氏崩。

translations.literal: Ninth month, guichou day: Empress Dowager Wenming, the Feng clan, died.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou in the ninth month, Empress Dowager Wenming, Lady Feng, died.

sentences.zh: 十五年正月癸亥晦，日有蝕之。

translations.literal: Fifteenth year, first month, guihai last day of the month: there was an eclipse of the sun.
translations.idiomatic: On the last day of the first month of the fifteenth year, a solar eclipse occurred.

sentences.zh: 占曰「王者將兵，天下擾動」。

translations.literal: Prognostication: "The king will lead troops, and all under Heaven will be thrown into turmoil."
translations.idiomatic: The prognostication read: "The ruler will take the field, and the realm will be thrown into turmoil."

sentences.zh: 十七年六月丙戌，高祖南伐。

translations.literal: Seventeenth year, sixth month, bingxu day: Emperor Xiaowen launched a southern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu in the sixth month of the seventeenth year, Emperor Xiaowen marched south.

sentences.zh: 十七年六月庚辰朔，日有蝕之。

translations.literal: Seventeenth year, sixth month, gengchen new moon: there was an eclipse of the sun.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengchen new moon in the sixth month of the seventeenth year, a solar eclipse occurred.

sentences.zh: 十八年五月甲戌朔，日有蝕之。

translations.literal: Eighteenth year, fifth month, jiaxu new moon: there was an eclipse of the sun.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiaxu new moon in the fifth month of the eighteenth year, a solar eclipse occurred.

sentences.zh: 二十年九月庚寅晦，日有蝕之。

translations.literal: Twentieth year, ninth month, gengyin last day of the month: there was an eclipse of the sun.
translations.idiomatic: On the last day of the ninth month of the twentieth year, a solar eclipse occurred.

sentences.zh: 二十三年六月己卯，日中有黑氣。

translations.literal: Twenty-third year, sixth month, jimao day: there was black vapor within the sun.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao in the sixth month of the twenty-third year, black vapor appeared within the sun.

sentences.zh: 占曰「內有逆謀」。

translations.literal: Prognostication: "Within there is treasonous plotting."
translations.idiomatic: The prognostication read: "Treason is plotting within."

sentences.zh: 八月癸亥，南徐州刺史沈陵南叛。

translations.literal: Eighth month, guihai day: Shen Ling, Governor of Southern Xuzhou, rebelled and fled south.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai in the eighth month, Shen Ling, governor of Southern Xuzhou, rebelled and fled south.

sentences.zh: 十二月甲申，日中有黑氣，大如桃。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, jiashen day: there was black vapor within the sun, as large as a peach.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen in the twelfth month, black vapor as large as a peach appeared within the sun.

sentences.zh: 世宗景明元年正月辛丑朔，日有蝕之。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanwu, Jingming first year, first month, xinchou new moon: there was an eclipse of the sun.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinchou new moon in the first month of Jingming 1, under Emperor Xuanwu, a solar eclipse occurred.

sentences.zh: 七月己亥朔，日有蝕之。

translations.literal: Seventh month, jihai new moon: there was an eclipse of the sun.
translations.idiomatic: On the jihai new moon in the seventh month, a solar eclipse occurred.

sentences.zh: 二年四月癸酉，日自午及未再暈，內黃外白。

translations.literal: Second year, fourth month, guiyou day: from the wu hour through the wei hour the sun was ringed by halos twice, yellow within and white without.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou in the fourth month of the second year, from the wu hour through the wei hour the sun was ringed twice by halos, yellow within and white without.

sentences.zh: 七月癸巳朔，日有蝕之。

translations.literal: Seventh month, guisi new moon: there was an eclipse of the sun.
translations.idiomatic: On the guisi new moon in the seventh month, a solar eclipse occurred.

sentences.zh: 八月戊辰，日赤無光，中有黑子一。

translations.literal: Eighth month, wuchen day: the sun was red and without light, with one black spot within it.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen in the eighth month, the sun turned red and dim, with one black spot upon it.

sentences.zh: 三年正月乙巳，日中有黑氣如鵝子，申、酉復見；

translations.literal: Third year, first month, yisi day: within the sun was black vapor like a goose egg; it was seen again at the shen and you hours;
translations.idiomatic: On yisi in the first month of the third year, black vapor like a goose egg appeared within the sun and was seen again at the shen and you hours;

sentences.zh: 又有二黑氣橫貫日。

translations.literal: there were also two black vapors crossing the sun horizontally.
translations.idiomatic: two black vapors also crossed the sun horizontally.

sentences.zh: 二月辛卯，日中有黑氣，大如鵝子。

translations.literal: Second month, xinmao day: within the sun was black vapor as large as a goose egg.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao in the second month, black vapor as large as a goose egg appeared within the sun.

sentences.zh: 七月丁巳朔，日有蝕之。

translations.literal: Seventh month, dingsi new moon: there was an eclipse of the sun.
translations.idiomatic: On the dingsi new moon in the seventh month, a solar eclipse occurred.

sentences.zh: 正始元年十二月丙戌，黑氣貫日。

translations.literal: Zhengshi first year, twelfth month, bingxu day: black vapor pierced the sun.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu in the twelfth month of Zhengshi 1, black vapor pierced the sun.

sentences.zh: 壬子，日有冠珥，內黃外青。

translations.literal: Renzi day: the sun had a crown and luminous appendages, yellow within and green without.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi, the sun wore a crown and luminous appendages, yellow within and green without.

sentences.zh: 占曰「天下喜」。

translations.literal: Prognostication: "All under Heaven will rejoice."
translations.idiomatic: The prognostication read: "The realm will rejoice."

sentences.zh: 三年正月丁卯，皇子生，大赦天下。

translations.literal: Third year, first month, dingmao day: an imperial son was born, and a great amnesty was proclaimed throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao in the first month of the third year, an imperial son was born and a great amnesty was proclaimed throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 三年二月甲辰，日左右有珥，內赤外黃。

translations.literal: Third year, second month, jiachen day: to the left and right of the sun were luminous appendages, red within and yellow without.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen in the second month of the third year, luminous appendages appeared to the left and right of the sun, red within and yellow without.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，日暈，外白內黃。

translations.literal: Xinhai day: a solar halo, white without and yellow within.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai, the sun was ringed by a halo, white without and yellow within.

sentences.zh: 十月乙巳，日赤無光。

translations.literal: Tenth month, yisi day: the sun was red and without light.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi in the tenth month, the sun turned red and dim.

sentences.zh: 十二月乙卯，日暈，內黃外青，東西有珥，北有背。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, yimao day: a solar halo, yellow within and green without, with luminous appendages to east and west and a contrary halo to the north.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao in the twelfth month, the sun was ringed by a halo, yellow within and green without, with luminous appendages to the east and west and a contrary halo to the north.

sentences.zh: 巳時，白虹貫日。

translations.literal: At the si hour, a white rainbow pierced the sun.
translations.idiomatic: At the si hour, a white rainbow pierced the sun.

sentences.zh: 永平元年三月己酉，日南北有珥，外青內黃，暈不匝；

translations.literal: Yongping first year, third month, jiyou day: the sun had luminous appendages to north and south, green without and yellow within, and the halo did not complete the circuit;
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou in the third month of Yongping 1, luminous appendages appeared to the north and south of the sun, green without and yellow within, and the halo did not complete its ring;

sentences.zh: 西北有直氣，長尺餘；

translations.literal: to the northwest there was a straight vapor more than one chi long;
translations.idiomatic: to the northwest a straight vapor more than one chi long appeared;

sentences.zh: 北有白虹貫日。

translations.literal: to the north a white rainbow pierced the sun.
translations.idiomatic: to the north a white rainbow pierced the sun.

sentences.zh: 八月壬子朔，日有蝕之。

translations.literal: Eighth month, renzi new moon: there was an eclipse of the sun.
translations.idiomatic: On the renzi new moon in the eighth month, a solar eclipse occurred.

sentences.zh: 二年八月丙午朔，日有蝕之。

translations.literal: Second year, eighth month, bingwu new moon: there was an eclipse of the sun.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingwu new moon in the eighth month of the second year, a solar eclipse occurred.

sentences.zh: 丁卯旦，日旁有黑氣，形如月，從東南來衝日。

translations.literal: At dawn on dingmao day, beside the sun was black vapor in the shape of the moon, coming from the southeast to strike the sun.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn on dingmao, black vapor shaped like the moon came from the southeast and struck the sun.

sentences.zh: 如此者一辰，乃滅。

translations.literal: It remained thus for one double-hour period, then vanished.
translations.idiomatic: It remained thus for one double-hour, then vanished.

sentences.zh: 三年二月甲子，日中有黑氣二。

translations.literal: Third year, second month, jiazi day: within the sun were two black vapors.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi in the second month of the third year, two black vapors appeared within the sun.

sentences.zh: 十二月乙未，日交暈，中赤外黃，東西有珥，南北白暈貫日，皆匝。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, yiwei day: intersecting solar halos, red in the center and yellow without, with luminous appendages to east and west; white halos to north and south pierced the sun, all completing the circuit.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei in the twelfth month, intersecting solar halos appeared, red at the center and yellow without, with luminous appendages to the east and west; white halos to the north and south pierced the sun and completed the ring.

sentences.zh: 四年十一月癸卯，日中有黑氣二，大如桃。

translations.literal: Fourth year, eleventh month, guimao day: within the sun were two black vapors, as large as peaches.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao in the eleventh month of the fourth year, two black vapors as large as peaches appeared within the sun.

sentences.zh: 占曰「天子崩」。

translations.literal: Prognostication: "The Son of Heaven will die."
translations.idiomatic: The prognostication read: "The Son of Heaven will die."

sentences.zh: 延昌四年正月丁巳，世宗昇遐。

translations.literal: Yanchang fourth year, first month, dingsi day: Emperor Xuanwu ascended afar.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi in the first month of Yanchang 4, Emperor Xuanwu died.

sentences.zh: 十二月壬戌朔，日有蝕之，在牛四度。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, renxu new moon: there was an eclipse of the sun, at four degrees in the Ox.
translations.idiomatic: On the renxu new moon in the twelfth month, a solar eclipse occurred at four degrees in the Ox constellation.

sentences.zh: 占曰「其國叛兵發」。

translations.literal: Prognostication: "In that state rebel armies will arise."
translations.idiomatic: The prognostication read: "Rebel armies will rise in that state."

sentences.zh: 延昌二年二月庚辰，[4]蕭衍郁洲民徐玄明等斬送衍鎮北將軍、青冀二州刺史張稷首，以州內附。

translations.literal: Yanchang second year, second month, gengchen day: [4] Xu Xuanming of Yuzhou and others under Xiao Yan beheaded and sent the head of Yan's Defender of the North General and Governor of Qing and Ji Provinces, Zhang Ji, and submitted the province to allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen in the second month of Yanchang 2, [4] Xu Xuanming of Yuzhou and others under Liang emperor Xiao Yan beheaded Zhang Ji, Defender of the North and governor of Qing and Ji, sent his head north, and submitted the province.

sentences.zh: 延昌元年二月甲戌至于辛巳，日初出及將沒，赤白無光明。

translations.literal: Yanchang first year, second month, from jiaxu through xinsi: at the sun's first rising and as it was about to set, it was red and white without brightness.
translations.idiomatic: From jiaxu through xinsi in the second month of Yanchang 1, at sunrise and sunset the sun appeared red and white without brightness.

sentences.zh: 五月己未晦，日十五分蝕九。

translations.literal: Fifth month, jiwei last day of the month: the sun was eclipsed nine parts in fifteen.
translations.idiomatic: On the last day of the fifth month, the sun was eclipsed by nine-fifteenths of its disk.

sentences.zh: 占曰「大旱，民流千里」。

translations.literal: Prognostication: "Great drought; the people will flee a thousand li."
translations.idiomatic: The prognostication read: "Great drought; the people will flee a thousand li."

sentences.zh: 二年春，京師民饑，死者數萬口。

translations.literal: Second year, spring: the people of the capital suffered famine, and tens of thousands died.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the second year, famine struck the capital, and tens of thousands died.

sentences.zh: 二年閏月辛亥，日中有黑氣。

translations.literal: Second year, intercalary month, xinhai day: within the sun was black vapor.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai in the intercalary month of the second year, black vapor appeared within the sun.

sentences.zh: 占曰「內有逆謀」。

translations.literal: Prognostication: "Within there is treasonous plotting."
translations.idiomatic: The prognostication read: "Treason is plotting within."

sentences.zh: 三年十一月丁巳，幽州沙門劉僧紹聚眾反，自號淨居國明法王，州郡捕斬之。

translations.literal: Third year, eleventh month, dingsi day: the monk Liu Sengshao of You Province gathered a crowd in rebellion, styled himself Bright Dharma King of the Pure Dwelling State, and was captured and beheaded by the province and commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi in the eleventh month of the third year, the monk Liu Sengshao of You Province rallied rebels, proclaimed himself Bright Dharma King of the Pure Dwelling State, and was captured and beheaded by local authorities.

sentences.zh: 五月甲寅朔，日有蝕之，京師不見，恒州以聞。

translations.literal: Fifth month, jiayin new moon: there was an eclipse of the sun; it was not seen in the capital, and Heng Province reported it.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiayin new moon in the fifth month, a solar eclipse occurred. The capital did not see it; Heng Province reported the phenomenon.

sentences.zh: 三年三月庚申，日交暈，其色內赤黃，外青白；

translations.literal: Third year, third month, gengshen day: intersecting solar halos, their color red-yellow within and green-white without;
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen in the third month of the third year, intersecting solar halos appeared, red-yellow within and green-white without;

sentences.zh: 南北有佩，可長二丈許，內赤黃，外青白；

translations.literal: to north and south were pendant halos about two zhang long, red-yellow within and green-white without;
translations.idiomatic: to the north and south pendant halos about two zhang long appeared, red-yellow within and green-white without;

sentences.zh: 西有白暈貫日。

translations.literal: to the west a white halo pierced the sun.
translations.idiomatic: to the west a white halo pierced the sun.

sentences.zh: 又日東有一抱，長二丈許，內赤黃，外青。

translations.literal: Again, to the east of the sun was one embracing halo about two zhang long, red-yellow within and green without.
translations.idiomatic: East of the sun an embracing halo about two zhang long also appeared, red-yellow within and green without.

sentences.zh: 四月甲辰卯時，日暈帀；

translations.literal: Fourth month, jiachen day, mao hour: a solar halo completed the circuit;
translations.idiomatic: At the mao hour on jiachen in the fourth month, a solar halo completed its ring;

sentences.zh: 西有一背，內赤外黃；

translations.literal: to the west was one contrary halo, red within and yellow without;
translations.idiomatic: to the west a contrary halo appeared, red within and yellow without;

sentences.zh: 南北有珥，內赤外黃；

translations.literal: to north and south were luminous appendages, red within and yellow without;
translations.idiomatic: to the north and south luminous appendages appeared, red within and yellow without;

sentences.zh: 漸滅。

translations.literal: then gradually vanished.
translations.idiomatic: then gradually faded away.

sentences.zh: 十二月己酉，日暈，北有一抱，內赤外白，兩傍有珥，北有白虹貫日。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, jiyou day: a solar halo; to the north was one embracing halo, red within and white without, with luminous appendages to both sides, and to the north a white rainbow pierced the sun.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou in the twelfth month, the sun was ringed by a halo. To the north an embracing halo appeared, red within and white without, with luminous appendages on both sides, and a white rainbow pierced the sun from the north.

sentences.zh: 神龜元年三月丁丑，白虹貫日。

translations.literal: Shengui first year, third month, dingchou day: a white rainbow pierced the sun.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou in the third month of Shengui 1, a white rainbow pierced the sun.

sentences.zh: 占曰「天下有來臣之眾，不三年」。

translations.literal: Prognostication: "All under Heaven will have a multitude of coming subjects, within no more than three years."
translations.idiomatic: The prognostication read: "Subjects will come in from across the realm, within three years."

sentences.zh: 十一月乙酉，[5]蠕蠕莫緣梁賀侯豆率男女七百口來降。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, yiyou day: [5] Moyuanliang Hehoudou of the Rouran led seven hundred men and women in submission.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou in the eleventh month, [5] Moyuanliang Hehoudou of the Rouran led seven hundred men and women in submission.

sentences.zh: 二年正月辛巳朔，日有蝕之。

translations.literal: Second year, first month, xinsi new moon: there was an eclipse of the sun.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinsi new moon in the first month of the second year, a solar eclipse occurred.

sentences.zh: 正光元年正月乙亥朔，日有蝕之。

translations.literal: Zhengguang first year, first month, yihai new moon: there was an eclipse of the sun.
translations.idiomatic: On the yihai new moon in the first month of Zhengguang 1, a solar eclipse occurred.

sentences.zh: 占曰「有大臣亡」。

translations.literal: Prognostication: "A great minister will perish."
translations.idiomatic: The prognostication read: "A great minister will perish."

sentences.zh: 七月丙子，殺太傅、領太尉、清河王懌。

translations.literal: Seventh month, bingzi day: Yuan Yi, Grand Tutor, Concurrent Grand Commandant, and Prince of Qinghe, was killed.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi in the seventh month, Yuan Yi, Prince of Qinghe, Grand Tutor and concurrent Grand Commandant, was executed.

sentences.zh: 二年五月丁酉，日有蝕之，夏州以聞。

translations.literal: Second year, fifth month, dingyou day: there was an eclipse of the sun; Xia Province reported it.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou in the fifth month of the second year, a solar eclipse occurred. Xia Province reported the phenomenon.

sentences.zh: 三年正月甲寅，日交暈，內赤外青，有白虹貫暈；

translations.literal: Third year, first month, jiayin day: intersecting solar halos, red within and green without, with a white rainbow piercing the halo;
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin in the first month of the third year, intersecting solar halos appeared, red within and green without, and a white rainbow pierced the halo;

sentences.zh: 外有直氣，長二丈許，內赤外青。

translations.literal: without was a straight vapor about two zhang long, red within and green without.
translations.idiomatic: outside was a straight vapor about two zhang long, red within and green without.

sentences.zh: 五月壬辰朔，日有蝕之。

translations.literal: Fifth month, renchen new moon: there was an eclipse of the sun.
translations.idiomatic: On the renchen new moon in the fifth month, a solar eclipse occurred.

sentences.zh: 占曰「秦邦不臣」。

translations.literal: Prognostication: "The Qin region will not be loyal."
translations.idiomatic: The prognostication read: "The Qin region will rebel."

sentences.zh: 五年六月，秦州城人莫折大提據城反，自稱秦王。

translations.literal: Fifth year, sixth month: Mozhe Dati of Qinzhou, a townsman of the city, seized the city in rebellion and styled himself King of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the fifth year, Mozhe Dati of Qinzhou seized the city in rebellion and proclaimed himself King of Qin.

sentences.zh: 十月己巳，太史奏自八月已來，黃埃掩日，日出三丈，色赤如赭，無光曜。

translations.literal: Tenth month, jisi day: the Grand Astrologer reported that from the eighth month onward yellow dust veiled the sun; when the sun rose three zhang high, its color was red as ochre and without radiance.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi in the tenth month, the Grand Astrologer reported that since the eighth month yellow dust had veiled the sun; when it rose three zhang high, it was red as ochre and without radiance.

sentences.zh: 十一月己丑朔，日有蝕之。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, jichou new moon: there was an eclipse of the sun.
translations.idiomatic: On the jichou new moon in the eleventh month, a solar eclipse occurred.

sentences.zh: 占曰「有小兵，在西北」。

translations.literal: Prognostication: "There will be minor warfare in the northwest."
translations.idiomatic: The prognostication read: "Minor warfare will arise in the northwest."

sentences.zh: 四年二月己卯，蠕蠕主阿那瓌率眾犯塞。

translations.literal: Fourth year, second month, jimao day: the Rouran ruler Anagui led his forces in violation of the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao in the second month of the fourth year, the Rouran ruler Anagui led his forces in an attack on the frontier.

sentences.zh: 四年十一月癸未朔，日有蝕之。

translations.literal: Fourth year, eleventh month, guiwei new moon: there was an eclipse of the sun.
translations.idiomatic: On the guiwei new moon in the eleventh month of the fourth year, a solar eclipse occurred.

sentences.zh: 五年閏月乙酉，日暈，內赤外青；

translations.literal: Fifth year, intercalary month, yiyou day: a solar halo, red within and green without;
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou in the intercalary month of the fifth year, the sun was ringed by a halo, red within and green without;

sentences.zh: 南有珥，上有一抱兩背，內赤外青。

translations.literal: to the south were luminous appendages; above were one embracing halo and two contrary halos, red within and green without.
translations.idiomatic: to the south luminous appendages appeared; above were one embracing halo and two contrary halos, red within and green without.

sentences.zh: 十二月丙申，日暈，南北有珥，上有兩抱一背。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, bingshen day: a solar halo, with luminous appendages to north and south; above were two embracing halos and one contrary halo.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen in the twelfth month, the sun was ringed by a halo with luminous appendages to the north and south; above were two embracing halos and one contrary halo.

sentences.zh: 孝昌元年十二月丙戌，白虹刺日不過，虹中有一背。

translations.literal: Xiaochang first year, twelfth month, bingxu day: a white rainbow stabbed at the sun but did not pass through; within the rainbow was one contrary halo.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu in the twelfth month of Xiaochang 1, a white rainbow struck at the sun but did not pass through; within the rainbow was one contrary halo.

sentences.zh: 占曰「有臣背其主」，一曰「有反城」。

translations.literal: Prognostication: "A minister will turn against his lord"; alternatively, "There will be a rebellious city."
translations.idiomatic: The prognostication read: "A minister will turn against his lord," or alternatively, "A city will rebel."

sentences.zh: 三年九月己卯，[6]東豫州刺史元慶和據城南叛。

translations.literal: Third year, ninth month, jimao day: [6] Yuan Qinghe, Governor of Eastern Yuzhou, seized the city and rebelled to the south.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao in the ninth month of the third year, [6] Yuan Qinghe, governor of Eastern Yuzhou, seized the city and rebelled southward.

sentences.zh: 三年十一月戊寅辰時，日暈，東面不合，其色內赤外黃；

translations.literal: Third year, eleventh month, wuyin day, chen hour: a solar halo, incomplete on the eastern side, its color red within and yellow without;
translations.idiomatic: At the chen hour on wuyin in the eleventh month of the third year, a solar halo appeared, incomplete on the eastern side, red within and yellow without;

sentences.zh: 東西有珥，內赤外黃；

translations.literal: to east and west were luminous appendages, red within and yellow without;
translations.idiomatic: to the east and west luminous appendages appeared, red within and yellow without;

sentences.zh: 西北去暈一尺餘，有一背，長二丈餘，廣三尺許，內赤外黃。

translations.literal: to the northwest, more than one chi from the halo, was one contrary halo more than two zhang long and about three chi wide, red within and yellow without.
translations.idiomatic: more than one chi northwest of the halo, a contrary halo more than two zhang long and about three chi wide appeared, red within and yellow without.

sentences.zh: 莊帝永安二年三月甲戌未時，日暈三重，內黃赤，外青白，暈東西兩處不合，其狀如抱。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaozhuang, Yong'an second year, third month, jiaxu day, wei hour: a triple solar halo, yellow-red within and green-white without; the halo was incomplete in two places to east and west, its form like an embrace.
translations.idiomatic: At the wei hour on jiaxu in the third month of Yong'an 2, under Emperor Xiaozhuang, a triple solar halo appeared, yellow-red within and green-white without; the halo was incomplete in two places to the east and west, shaped like an embrace.

sentences.zh: 五月辛酉，日暈，東西兩處不合。

translations.literal: Fifth month, xinyou day: a solar halo, incomplete in two places to east and west.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou in the fifth month, the sun was ringed by a halo incomplete in two places to the east and west.

sentences.zh: 辛未申時，日南有珥；

translations.literal: Xinwei day, shen hour: to the south of the sun were luminous appendages;
translations.idiomatic: At the shen hour on xinwei, luminous appendages appeared to the south of the sun;

sentences.zh: 去一尺餘有一背，長三丈許，廣五尺餘，內赤外青。

translations.literal: more than one chi away was one contrary halo about three zhang long and more than five chi wide, red within and green without.
translations.idiomatic: more than one chi away a contrary halo about three zhang long and more than five chi wide appeared, red within and green without.

sentences.zh: 七月丙寅，直東去日三尺許有一背，長二丈餘，內赤外青。

translations.literal: Seventh month, bingyin day: due east, about three chi from the sun, was one contrary halo more than two zhang long, red within and green without.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin in the seventh month, due east about three chi from the sun, a contrary halo more than two zhang long appeared, red within and green without.

sentences.zh: 半食頃，從北頭漸滅至半，須臾還如初見，內赤外青，其色分炳。

translations.literal: After the span of half a meal, from the northern end it gradually vanished to the halfway point; in a moment it returned as at first sight, red within and green without, its colors clearly distinct.
translations.idiomatic: After half a meal's time it faded from the northern end to the midpoint; in a moment it returned as at first, red within and green without, its colors clearly distinct.

sentences.zh: 十月己酉朔，日從地下蝕出，十五分蝕七，虧從西南角起。

translations.literal: Tenth month, jiyou new moon: the sun emerged from eclipse below the earth; it was eclipsed seven parts in fifteen, and the waning began from the southwestern corner.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiyou new moon in the tenth month, the sun emerged from eclipse below the horizon, eclipsed by seven-fifteenths of its disk, with the shadow beginning from the southwestern corner.

sentences.zh: 占曰「西夷欲殺，後有大兵，必西行」。

translations.literal: Prognostication: "Western barbarians wish to kill; afterward there will be great armies, and they will surely march west."
translations.idiomatic: The prognostication read: "Western barbarians seek bloodshed; afterward great armies will march, and they will surely advance west."

sentences.zh: 三年四月丁卯，雍州刺史尒朱天光討擒万俟醜奴、蕭寶夤於安定，送京師斬之。

translations.literal: Third year, fourth month, dingmao day: Erzhu Tianguang, Governor of Yong Province, campaigned against and captured Mozhe Chounu and Xiao Baoyin at Anding, sent them to the capital, and beheaded them.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao in the fourth month of the third year, Erzhu Tianguang, governor of Yong Province, captured Mozhe Chounu and Xiao Baoyin at Anding, sent them to the capital, and had them beheaded.

sentences.zh: 三年五月戊戌辰時，日暈帀，內赤外白，暈內有兩珥；

translations.literal: Third year, fifth month, wuxu day, chen hour: a solar halo completed the circuit, red within and white without, with two luminous appendages within the halo;
translations.idiomatic: At the chen hour on wuxu in the fifth month of the third year, a solar halo completed its ring, red within and white without, with two luminous appendages within the halo;

sentences.zh: 西有白虹貫日；

translations.literal: to the west a white rainbow pierced the sun;
translations.idiomatic: to the west a white rainbow pierced the sun;

sentences.zh: 東北有一背，內赤外青；

translations.literal: to the northeast was one contrary halo, red within and green without;
translations.idiomatic: to the northeast one contrary halo appeared, red within and green without;

sentences.zh: 南有一背，內赤外青；

translations.literal: to the south was one contrary halo, red within and green without;
translations.idiomatic: to the south one contrary halo appeared, red within and green without;

sentences.zh: 東有一抱，內青外赤。

translations.literal: to the east was one embracing halo, green within and red without.
translations.idiomatic: to the east one embracing halo appeared, green within and red without.

sentences.zh: 京師不見，青州表聞。

translations.literal: It was not seen in the capital; Qing Province reported it by memorial.
translations.idiomatic: The capital did not see it; Qing Province reported the phenomenon by memorial.

sentences.zh: 六月辛丑，日暈，白虹貫日。

translations.literal: Sixth month, xinchou day: a solar halo, and a white rainbow pierced the sun.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou in the sixth month, the sun was ringed by a halo, and a white rainbow pierced it.

sentences.zh: 前廢帝普泰元年三月丁亥，日月並赤赭色，天地溷濁。

translations.literal: Deposed Emperor Jiemin, Putai first year, third month, dinghai day: the sun and moon were both red-ochre in color, and heaven and earth were murky and turbid.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai in the third month of Putai 1, under the Deposed Emperor Jiemin, the sun and moon both turned red-ochre, and heaven and earth grew murky and dim.

sentences.zh: 六月己亥朔，日蝕從西南角起，雲陰不見，定相二州表聞。

translations.literal: Sixth month, jihai new moon: the solar eclipse began from the southwestern corner; cloud and shade obscured it from view, and Ding and Xiang Provinces reported it by memorial.
translations.idiomatic: On the jihai new moon in the sixth month, the eclipse began from the southwestern corner. Clouds hid it from view; Ding and Xiang Provinces reported the phenomenon by memorial.

sentences.zh: 占曰「主弱，小人持政」。

translations.literal: Prognostication: "The ruler is weak; petty men hold power."
translations.idiomatic: The prognostication read: "The ruler is weak, and petty men hold power."

sentences.zh: 時尒朱世隆兄弟專擅威福。

translations.literal: At that time the Erzhu brothers Shilong monopolized authority and favor.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Erzhu Shilong and his brothers monopolized power and favor.

sentences.zh: 後廢帝中興二年二月辛丑辰時，日暈，東西不合，其色內赤外青；

translations.literal: Deposed Emperor Xiaojing, Zhongxing second year, second month, xinchou day, chen hour: a solar halo, incomplete to east and west, its color red within and green without;
translations.idiomatic: At the chen hour on xinchou in the second month of Zhongxing 2, under the Deposed Emperor Xiaojing, a solar halo appeared, incomplete to the east and west, red within and green without;

sentences.zh: 南北有珥；

translations.literal: to north and south were luminous appendages;
translations.idiomatic: to the north and south luminous appendages appeared;

sentences.zh: 西北去暈一尺餘有一背，長二丈許，可廣三尺，內赤外青。

translations.literal: to the northwest, more than one chi from the halo, was one contrary halo about two zhang long and about three chi wide, red within and green without.
translations.idiomatic: more than one chi northwest of the halo, a contrary halo about two zhang long and about three chi wide appeared, red within and green without.

sentences.zh: 十一月，日暈再重；

translations.literal: Eleventh month: a double solar halo;
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, a double solar halo appeared;

sentences.zh: 上有背，長三丈餘，內青外赤。

translations.literal: above was a contrary halo more than three zhang long, green within and red without.
translations.idiomatic: above it a contrary halo more than three zhang long appeared, green within and red without.

sentences.zh: 出帝太昌元年五月，日暈再重；

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu, Taichang first year, fifth month: a double solar halo;
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of Taichang 1, under Emperor Xiaowu, a double solar halo appeared;

sentences.zh: 上有兩背，一尺許。

translations.literal: above were two contrary halos about one chi in size.
translations.idiomatic: above were two contrary halos about one chi in size.

sentences.zh: 癸丑午時，日南有珥；

translations.literal: Guichou day, wu hour: to the south of the sun were luminous appendages;
translations.idiomatic: At the wu hour on guichou, luminous appendages appeared to the south of the sun;

sentences.zh: 去日一尺餘有一背，長三丈許，廣五尺，內赤外青。

translations.literal: more than one chi from the sun was one contrary halo about three zhang long and five chi wide, red within and green without.
translations.idiomatic: more than one chi from the sun, a contrary halo about three zhang long and five chi wide appeared, red within and green without.

sentences.zh: 十月辛酉朔，日從地下蝕出，虧從西南角起。

translations.literal: Tenth month, xinyou new moon: the sun emerged from eclipse below the earth, and the waning began from the southwestern corner.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinyou new moon in the tenth month, the sun emerged from eclipse below the horizon, with the shadow beginning from the southwestern corner.

sentences.zh: 占曰「有兵大行」。

translations.literal: Prognostication: "Armies will march on a great scale."
translations.idiomatic: The prognostication read: "Armies will march on a great scale."

sentences.zh: 永熙二年正月甲午，齊獻武王自晉陽出討尒朱兆。

translations.literal: Yongxi second year, first month, jiawu day: the Qi Prince Xianwu marched out from Jinyang to campaign against Erzhu Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu in the first month of Yongxi 2, Prince Xianwu of Qi marched out from Jinyang to campaign against Erzhu Zhao.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，大破之於赤洪嶺，兆遁走自殺。

translations.literal: Dingyou day: he inflicted a great defeat upon him at Chihong Ridge; Zhao fled and killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou he routed Zhao decisively at Chihong Ridge. Zhao fled and took his own life.

sentences.zh: 永熙二年四月己未朔，日有蝕之，在丙，虧從正南起。

translations.literal: Yongxi second year, fourth month, jiwei new moon: there was an eclipse of the sun, at the bing position; the waning began from due south.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiwei new moon in the fourth month of Yongxi 2, a solar eclipse occurred at the bing position, with the shadow beginning from due south.

sentences.zh: 占曰「君陰謀」。

translations.literal: Prognostication: "The ruler plots in secret."
translations.idiomatic: The prognostication read: "The ruler plots in secret."

sentences.zh: 三年五月辛卯，出帝為斛斯椿等諸佞關構，猜於齊獻武王，託討蕭衍，盛暑徵發河南諸州之兵，天下怪惡之。

translations.literal: Third year, fifth month, xinmao day: Emperor Xiaowu, because the various flatterers such as Husu Chun slandered and incited discord, became suspicious of the Qi Prince Xianwu; he used a campaign against Xiao Yan as a pretext and, in the height of summer, summoned the armies of the Henan commanderies. All under Heaven regarded this with horror and loathing.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao in the fifth month of the third year, flatterers led by Husu Chun turned Emperor Xiaowu against Prince Xianwu of Qi. He used a campaign against Xiao Yan as a pretext and, in the height of summer, mobilized the armies of the Henan commanderies. The realm regarded this with horror and loathing.

sentences.zh: 語在斛斯椿傳。

translations.literal: The account is in the biography of Husu Chun.
translations.idiomatic: The full account appears in the biography of Husu Chun.

sentences.zh: 三年四月癸丑，日有蝕之。

translations.literal: Third year, fourth month, guichou day: there was an eclipse of the sun.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou in the fourth month of the third year, a solar eclipse occurred.

sentences.zh: 占曰「有亂殺天子者」。

translations.literal: Prognostication: "There will be disorder, and someone will kill the Son of Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: The prognostication read: "Rebellion will arise, and the Son of Heaven will be killed."

sentences.zh: 七月丁未，出帝為斛斯椿等迫脅，遂出於長安。

translations.literal: Seventh month, dingwei day: Emperor Xiaowu, compelled and coerced by Husu Chun and others, thereupon departed for Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei in the seventh month, Husu Chun and his faction forced Emperor Xiaowu to flee to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 二年二月己丑巳時，日暈帀，白虹貫日不徹。

translations.literal: Second year, second month, jichou day, si hour: a solar halo completed the circuit; a white rainbow pierced the sun but did not pass through.
translations.idiomatic: At the si hour on jichou in the second month of the second year, a solar halo completed its ring, and a white rainbow pierced the sun but did not pass through.

sentences.zh: 興和二年閏月丁丑朔，日有蝕之。

translations.literal: Xinghe second year, intercalary month, dingchou new moon: there was an eclipse of the sun.
translations.idiomatic: On the dingchou new moon in the intercalary month of Xinghe 2, a solar eclipse occurred.

sentences.zh: 占曰「有小兵」。

translations.literal: Prognostication: "There will be minor warfare."
translations.idiomatic: The prognostication read: "Minor warfare will arise."

sentences.zh: 七月癸巳，元寶炬廣豫二州行臺趙繼宗、南青州刺史崔康寇陽翟，鎮將擊走之。

translations.literal: Seventh month, guisi day: Zhao Jizong of the Eastern Garrison of Guang and Yu Provinces under Yuan Baoju, and Cui Kang, Governor of Southern Qing Province, raided Yangdi; the garrison commander drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi in the seventh month, Zhao Jizong of the Guang-Yu garrison under Yuan Baoju and Cui Kang, governor of Southern Qing, raided Yangdi. The garrison commander drove them off.

sentences.zh: 武定三年冬十一月壬申，日暈兩重，東南角不合；

translations.literal: Wuding third year, winter, eleventh month, renshen day: a double solar halo, incomplete at the southeastern corner;
translations.idiomatic: On renshen in the eleventh month of winter in Wuding 3, a double solar halo appeared, incomplete at the southeastern corner;

sentences.zh: 西南、東北有珥；

translations.literal: to the southwest and northeast were luminous appendages;
translations.idiomatic: to the southwest and northeast luminous appendages appeared;

sentences.zh: 西北有兩重背；

translations.literal: to the northwest were two layers of contrary halos;
translations.idiomatic: to the northwest two layers of contrary halos appeared;

sentences.zh: 東北、西北有白氣，并有兩珥；

translations.literal: to the northeast and northwest were white vapors, and there were also two luminous appendages;
translations.idiomatic: to the northeast and northwest white vapors appeared, with two luminous appendages as well;

sentences.zh: 中間有一白氣，東西撗至珥。

translations.literal: in the middle was one white vapor stretching east and west to the appendages.
translations.idiomatic: in the middle one white vapor stretched east and west to the appendages.

sentences.zh: 十二月乙酉，竟天微有白雲，日暈，東南角不合；

translations.literal: Twelfth month, yiyou day: across the whole sky there were faint white clouds; a solar halo, incomplete at the southeastern corner;
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou in the twelfth month, faint white clouds covered the sky. A solar halo appeared, incomplete at the southeastern corner;

sentences.zh: 西南、東北有珥；

translations.literal: to the southwest and northeast were luminous appendages;
translations.idiomatic: to the southwest and northeast luminous appendages appeared;

sentences.zh: 西北有一背，去日一尺。

translations.literal: to the northwest was one contrary halo one chi from the sun.
translations.idiomatic: to the northwest one contrary halo appeared one chi from the sun.

sentences.zh: 三月辛丑，日暈帀，西北交暈貫日，并有一珥一抱。

translations.literal: Third month, xinchou day: a solar halo completed the circuit; intersecting halos to the northwest pierced the sun, and there were also one luminous appendage and one embracing halo.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou in the third month, a solar halo completed its ring. Intersecting halos to the northwest pierced the sun, with one luminous appendage and one embracing halo as well.

sentences.zh: 六年七月庚寅朔，日有蝕之，虧從西北角起。

translations.literal: Sixth year, seventh month, gengyin new moon: there was an eclipse of the sun, and the waning began from the northwestern corner.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengyin new moon in the seventh month of the sixth year, a solar eclipse occurred, with the shadow beginning from the northwestern corner.

sentences.zh: 校勘記

translations.literal: Collation Notes
translations.idiomatic: Collation Notes

sentences.zh: 高祖延興元年十二月癸卯日有蝕之 按是年十二月乙酋朔，癸卯是十九日，不應有日蝕。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen, Yanxing first year, twelfth month, guimao day, there was an eclipse of the sun. Examination shows that in that year the twelfth month had a yiyou new moon; guimao was the nineteenth day, and there should not have been a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: The entry for a solar eclipse on guimao in the twelfth month of Yanxing 1 is doubtful. That month began on yiyou; guimao was the nineteenth day, when no solar eclipse should have occurred.

sentences.zh: 三年十二月癸卯朔日有蝕之四年正月癸酋朔日有蝕之 按無連續兩月日蝕之理，必有誤。

translations.literal: Third year, twelfth month, guimao new moon, there was an eclipse of the sun; fourth year, first month, guiyou new moon, there was an eclipse of the sun. Examination shows that there is no principle by which eclipses should occur in two successive months; there must be an error.
translations.idiomatic: Entries for solar eclipses on the guimao new moon in the twelfth month of the third year and the guiyou new moon in the first month of the fourth year cannot both be correct, since two eclipses in successive months are impossible. The dates must be wrong.

sentences.zh: 二月乙酋晦日有蝕之 按太和二年二月己卯朔，乙酋乃七日，晦日值丁未。

translations.literal: Second month, yiyou last day of the month, there was an eclipse of the sun. Examination shows that in Taihe second year the second month had a jimao new moon; yiyou was the seventh day, and the last day of the month fell on dingwei.
translations.idiomatic: The entry for a solar eclipse on the last day of the second month, yiyou, is doubtful. In Taihe 2 the second month began on jimao; yiyou was only the seventh day, and the last day of the month was dingwei.

sentences.zh: 必有誤。

translations.literal: There must be an error.
translations.idiomatic: The date must be wrong.

sentences.zh: 延昌二年二月庚辰 諸本「二月」作「正月」。

translations.literal: Yanchang second year, second month, gengchen. In various editions "second month" reads "first month."
translations.idiomatic: Yanchang 2, second month, gengchen: various editions read "first month" for "second month."

sentences.zh: 按卷八世宗紀，事在是年二月庚辰。

translations.literal: Examination of fascicle 8, the Basic Annals of Emperor Xuanwu, shows that the event was in the gengchen day of the second month of that year.
translations.idiomatic: The Basic Annals of Emperor Xuanwu in fascicle 8 place the event on gengchen in the second month of that year.

sentences.zh: 是年正月丙戊朔，無庚辰，二月丙辰朔，庚辰乃二十五日。

translations.literal: In that year the first month had a bingxu new moon, and there was no gengchen; the second month had a bingchen new moon, and gengchen was the twenty-fifth day.
translations.idiomatic: That year's first month began on bingxu, so there was no gengchen in the first month. The second month began on bingchen, and gengchen was its twenty-fifth day.

sentences.zh: 這裏「正月」乃「二月」之訛。

translations.literal: Here "first month" is an error for "second month."
translations.idiomatic: Here "first month" is a scribal error for "second month."

sentences.zh: 今據紀改。

translations.literal: Now it is corrected according to the annals.
translations.idiomatic: The text is corrected here according to the annals.

sentences.zh: 十一月乙酉 按卷九肅宗紀，事在神龜二年十一月乙酋。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, yiyou. Examination of fascicle 9, the Basic Annals of Emperor Xiaozong, shows that the event was in Shengui second year, eleventh month, yiyou.
translations.idiomatic: Eleventh month, yiyou: the Basic Annals of Emperor Xiaozong in fascicle 9 place the event in the eleventh month of Shengui 2, on yiyou.

sentences.zh: 這裏「十一月」上脫「二年」二字。

translations.literal: Here the two characters "second year" are missing above "eleventh month."
translations.idiomatic: Here the words "second year" are missing before "eleventh month."

sentences.zh: 三年九月己卯 諸本「三年」作「二年」。

translations.literal: Third year, ninth month, jimao. In various editions "third year" reads "second year."
translations.idiomatic: Third year, ninth month, jimao: various editions read "second year" for "third year."

sentences.zh: 按卷九肅宗紀，事在孝昌三年九月辛卯，梁書卷五武帝紀三，在梁大通元年

translations.literal: Examination of fascicle 9, the Basic Annals of Emperor Xiaozong, shows that the event was in Xiaochang third year, ninth month, xinmao; the Basic Annals of Emperor Wu in fascicle 5 of the History of Liang places it in Datong first year of Liang
translations.idiomatic: The Basic Annals of Emperor Xiaozong in fascicle 9 place the event in the ninth month of Xiaochang 3, on xinmao, while the Basic Annals of Emperor Wu in fascicle 5 of the History of Liang place it in Liang Datong 1

sentences.zh: 〈即魏孝昌三年〉

translations.literal: (that is, Wei Xiaochang third year)
translations.idiomatic: (that is, Wei Xiaochang 3)

sentences.zh: 十月。

translations.literal: tenth month.
translations.idiomatic: in the tenth month.

sentences.zh: 記月不同，當是各據奏報，至元慶和降梁，必在孝昌三年無疑。

translations.literal: The recorded months differ; this should be because each source relied on its own memorial report. As for Yuan Qinghe's submission to Liang, it must without doubt have been in Xiaochang third year.
translations.idiomatic: The months differ because each source relied on its own memorial report. Yuan Qinghe's surrender to Liang must in any case have occurred in Xiaochang 3.

sentences.zh: 這裏「二」字乃「三」之訛。

translations.literal: Here the character "two" is an error for "three."
translations.idiomatic: Here "two" is a scribal error for "three."

sentences.zh: 今據紀改。

translations.literal: Now it is corrected according to the annals.
translations.idiomatic: The text is corrected here according to the annals.

sentences.zh: 是年九月有「己卯」，無「辛卯」，則是紀誤。

translations.literal: In that year the ninth month had "jimao" but not "xinmao"; therefore the annals are in error.
translations.idiomatic: That year's ninth month had a jimao day but no xinmao day, so the annals are wrong.
